outcome: Perinatal mortality and severe neonatal morbidity
cohort: 181,810 twin pregnancies without congenital anomalies delivered at 32-41 weeks gestation
finding: The study found that cesarean delivery may be beneficial for perinatal outcomes in twin pregnancies at or after 36 weeks gestation, while vaginal delivery might be preferable at 32 and 33 weeks.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with lower risk of the combined outcome (perinatal death and severe neonatal morbidity) compared to vaginal delivery at 36 weeks of gestation and beyond, even when restricted to different-sex twins.
